title: Riff, Rhythm, and Harmony Construction
description: How the music is built: riff cells, tremolo, chromatic motion, pedal tones, blast and double-kick vocabulary, song structure. Assumes music-theory foundations rather than reteaching intervals.

sourceReferences.title: Berklee Metal Guitar
sourceReferences.notes: Riff vocabulary, rhythm, modes, and right-hand technique as construction skills. Depends on fundamentals rather than reteaching intervals.

sourceReferences.title: MIT Heavy Metal 101
sourceReferences.notes: Songwriting tropes and technique as construction, not celebrity.

sourceReferences.title: Berklee Guitar Fundamentals
sourceReferences.notes: This course must not duplicate interval and meter literacy.

modules.title: Riff vocabulary
learningObjectives: Write a short cell that can be repeated, displaced, or mutated
Use mute, tremolo, pedal, and tuning as orchestration, not decoration

modules.title: Rhythm-section grammar
learningObjectives: Use blast, double-kick, and odd grouping as grammar
Put guitar and kit in different meters that coincide later

modules.title: Putting a song together
modules.blurb: Structure, two guitars, vocals as rhythm.
learningObjectives: Order cells so the song has contrast, not just density
Write two guitars or a vocal as rhythm, not as a pop hook

concepts.name: The riff cell
concepts.summary: A short figure that can be repeated, displaced, or mutated.
objectives: Write a short figure that can be repeated, displaced, or mutated
Identify the cell in a recorded riff before naming the band

concepts.name: Tremolo writing
concepts.summary: Picking that turns a pitch into a surface.
objectives: Use tremolo picking to turn a pitch into a surface
Write a tremolo line that still has a harmonic job

concepts.name: Chromatic movement
concepts.summary: Semitone steps as the riff's spine.
objectives: Use semitone steps as the riff's spine
Sequence a chromatic cell without turning it into a scale exercise

concepts.name: Pedal tones
concepts.summary: An open string that the cell grinds against.
objectives: Grind the cell against an open string
Release the pedal so the clash has a form

concepts.name: Death-metal harmony
concepts.summary: Diminished cells, chromatic planing, and riff as form.
objectives: Build harmony from diminished cells, chromatic planing, and riff-as-form
Analyze a section by the cell and the drum texture, not by V–I

concepts.name: Diminished cells
concepts.summary: Minor thirds stacked until the octave repeats.
objectives: Stack minor thirds until the octave repeats
Write a diminished cell that sequences instead of running

concepts.name: Tritone and flat-2 riffs
concepts.summary: The two intervals this style treats as home.
objectives: Treat tritone and flat-2 as home intervals for this style
Write a riff that sits on those intervals without borrowing a Phrygian lecture

concepts.name: Palm mute as orchestration
concepts.summary: Choked versus open as two instruments.
objectives: Use choked versus open as two instruments
Orchestrate a cell by mute, not by adding notes

concepts.name: Tunings that change the riff
concepts.summary: A dropped string is a compositional choice.
objectives: Choose a tuning because it changes the riff, not because it is 'heavier'
Predict the new open-string pedal a drop creates

concepts.name: Right-hand endurance versus accent
concepts.summary: Speed that still has a downbeat.
objectives: Keep a downbeat inside speed
Write an accent pattern a right hand can survive

concepts.name: Blast beats
concepts.summary: The drum grammar that made death metal possible.
objectives: Use a blast as a grid that removes the rock backbeat as the only accent
Contrast a blast section with a thrash d-beat as grammars

concepts.name: Blast vocabulary
concepts.summary: Traditional, bomb, hammer — different occupations of the kit.
objectives: Distinguish traditional, bomb, and hammer blasts by what the kit is doing
Choose a blast type for a texture, not for a speed contest

concepts.name: Double-kick vocabulary
concepts.summary: Two feet as a subdivision engine.
objectives: Use two feet as a subdivision engine
Write a kick figure that locks a guitar cell instead of filling space

concepts.name: Rhythmic displacement
concepts.summary: The same cell, started on a different beat of the bar.
objectives: Start the same cell on a different beat of the bar
Predict how the blast grid reaccents that move

concepts.name: Odd meter in death metal
concepts.summary: Groupings that are felt, not counted out loud.
objectives: Group an odd bar so it is felt, not counted out loud
Write 5 or 7 as additive cells a kit can phrase

concepts.name: Polymeter in the band
concepts.summary: Guitar in 3, kit in 4, a coincidence later.
objectives: Put guitar in one meter and kit in another, with a coincidence later
Mark the bar where the two grids meet

concepts.name: String skipping and wide intervals
concepts.summary: Leaps that refuse stepwise comfort.
objectives: Leap so the line refuses stepwise comfort
Give a wide interval a harmonic job, not a gym job

concepts.name: Sweeps as function, not sport
concepts.summary: An arpeggio that has a harmonic job.
objectives: Use a sweep as an arpeggio that has a harmonic job
Refuse a sweep that only proves the right hand

concepts.name: Song structure
concepts.summary: Intro, riff A, riff B, return — or a through-composed stack.
objectives: Order intro, riff A, riff B, and return — or refuse return on purpose
Mark a section change that is only a drum texture

concepts.name: Riff as form
concepts.summary: The form is the order of cells and their mutations.
objectives: Treat the form as the order of cells and their mutations
Show a mutation that is the next section, not a new song

concepts.name: Breakdowns and whether they belong
concepts.summary: Half-time weight as contrast, or as a different genre arriving.
objectives: Use half-time weight as contrast, or refuse it as a different genre arriving
Predict when a breakdown erases the cell you were writing

concepts.name: Vocals as a rhythmic instrument
concepts.summary: Phrasing against the kick, not a melody sitting on top.
objectives: Phrase the vocal against the kick, not as a melody sitting on top
Write a vocal rhythm that is a third grid

concepts.name: Two-guitar writing
concepts.summary: Unison, harmony a third above, or a second riff.
objectives: Choose unison, a third above, or a second riff
Predict what distortion does to a close harmony between two guitars
